title: Divarasib versus first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors in previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC
journal: New England Journal of Medicine; ESMO 2026 late-breaking presentation
population: 338 adults with previously treated advanced/metastatic KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC; 167 assigned divarasib and 171 assigned sotorasib or adagrasib.
comparator: Sotorasib once daily or adagrasib twice daily, selected by investigator.
summary: Median OS 17.7 vs 12.0 months (HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.41–0.78; p=0.0005); median PFS 9.8 vs 5.7 months (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.44–0.76; p<0.0001). Twelve-month PFS 44% vs 24%; ORR 58% vs 32%.

absoluteEffect.nnt: Approx. 5 at 12 months from fixed-time PFS rates; not calculated from median PFS or HR.
absoluteEffect.toxicity: Serious treatment-related AEs 7.8% vs 15.2%; treatment-related discontinuation 4.8% vs 11.7%.

clinicalInterpretation: A phase III head-to-head trial showed improved PFS and OS over currently used KRAS G12C inhibitors. The 20-point difference in 12-month PFS corresponds to an approximate landmark NNT of 5. Serious treatment-related toxicity and discontinuation were lower despite longer exposure. Divarasib remains investigational at this evidence cut-off.
criticalReview: The important result is not simply longer median PFS: KRASCENDO 1 is a direct phase III comparison against approved KRAS G12C inhibitors and reports both PFS and OS superiority. The 20-point difference in 12-month PFS corresponds to an approximate landmark NNT of 5. Serious treatment-related toxicity and discontinuation were lower despite longer exposure. However, divarasib remains investigational; use depends on regulatory and guideline decisions.
